structured.answer: Clal (כלל) has the cheapest S&P 500 track in keren hishtalmut at 0.48% from savings, with Menora right behind at 0.49%. I'd go with Clal.

stuck.why: The first row (מור, 0.7%) looked like the top pick. The note saying the order is 'מהיקר לזול' sits at the far left end of the line and I almost missed it, so I almost took the most expensive as the best.
'עוד לא דווח' with an orange warning mark sits in the cheapest-at-the-bottom spot. I wasn't sure if it was cheaper or just missing a number.
Not sure whether 'אין' means zero fee from deposits or 'no data'.

findings.what: Sorted from most expensive to cheapest, so the cheapest is at the very bottom and the most expensive at the top looks like the top pick. The sort note sits at the far left end of the line.
findings.where: Line above the table and first row (מור 0.7%)

findings.what: The same 'מהחיסכון' / 'אין מההפקדות' words repeat in every row, so I re-read them each time just to find the one number that differs.
A row with 'עוד לא דווח' and a warning icon sits in the cheapest spot at the bottom, which makes the end of the list confusing and a bit scary.
Fees are only in percent. 0.48 vs 0.7 feels like nothing; a shekel amount would have meant something.
Ring charts with colours and percentages placed next to them, so I had to match dot colours to the ring. I didn't understand what they meant.
The Menora row is split across the scroll, so its fee and its name land on different screens.
findings.where: Bottom of screen 1 / top of screen 2
